thread:
maya: Heads-up — I ran onboarding evals for openembed-4-small and its quantized variants (q8_0, q4_0). Quick summary: q4_0 shows a noticeable drop vs fp16 on our semantic-qa-10k suite (recall@5 down ~3.9%). Posting full notes below.

eval-bot: Auto-eval summary for thread 1749801123:
```
model           variant   R@1    R@5    R@10   MAP    silhouette
openembed-4     fp16      0.721  0.874  0.912  0.635  0.432
openembed-4     q8_0      0.716  0.869  0.908  0.629  0.428
openembed-4     q4_0      0.691  0.835  0.887  0.597  0.381
dataset: semantic-qa-10k | n_queries=10,000 | knn=hnsw,cosine
```

maya: Full command I ran so you can reproduce: 
```
./eval_embeddings.py --model openembed-4-small \n  --variants fp16 q8_0 q4_0 \n  --dataset semantic-qa-10k \n  --metric recall@1,recall@5,recall@10,map \n  --index hnsw --space cosine --ef_search 128
```

kevin: Can you paste the failure examples? Also what index config? ef_build/ef_search?

maya: ef_build=200, ef_search=128, M=32. Failures (pairs where fp16 top1 but q4_0 misses):
```
q: "How to reset my API key?"
fp16 top1: "Regenerating API keys in Console -> Settings"
q4_0 top1: "Billing and invoices FAQ"

q: "Best practices for streaming responses"
fp16 top1: "Use smaller chunk sizes + backpressure"
q4_0 top1: "Rate limits and quotas"
```

alex: Not great. I also computed cluster metrics on the label groups (5k random). Silhouette drops from 0.432 -> 0.381 for q4_0. That aligns with semantic shuffling.

sophia: Did you try cosine vs dot? Quantization sometimes changes norm distribution; cosine+whitening can help.

maya: I tried both. Table (cosine vs dot, recall@5 for q4_0):
- cosine: 0.835
- dot:    0.818
So cosine is better here. I didn't apply whitening yet.

kevin: What about dimensionality reduction? We sometimes see q4 artifacts concentrated in tail dims. Try PCA->256 or OPQ.

maya: Good call. Running a quick PCA->256 + whiten + re-index now. Will post numbers in ~10m.

eval-bot: Job submitted: eval-job-1749801123-pca256 (eta ~ 7m).

alex: Also include recall@k delta per query-length bucket. My hypothesis: short queries (<6 tokens) degrade more after q4 quant.

maya: Running bucketed analysis as part of the job. Early peek: short queries R@5 drop 5.6% relative, medium (6-15 tokens) drop 3.1%, long (>15) drop 1.0%.

sophia: That supports the tail-dim hypothesis. If shorter queries have lower signal, quant noise moves nearest neighbor. Try temperature scaling on similarity? Or reranking top-50 with a cheap cross-encoder.

kevin: For rollout plan: can we ship q8_0 as default (small perf win, tiny drop) and gate q4_0 behind a canary with additional whitening? Also add sample checks in CI that fail if R@5 drops >2% vs baseline.

maya: Agreed. Proposed immediate actions:
- Add PCA(256)+whiten preproc for q4_0 candidates
- Canary q8_0 for general availability
- Add per-bucket recall test to embed-evals CI (thresholds: short:-4%, medium:-2%, long:-1%)
- Collect human eval on 200 random failures to check perceived relevance

eval-bot: PCA run finished. New results: 
```
openembed-4 q4_0 + PCA256+whiten | R@5 = 0.858 (+2.3% vs raw q4_0, +0.9% vs fp16)
silhouette = 0.412
```

maya: Nice — PCA+whiten recovers most of the gap. I'll prepare a PR that hooks PCA/whiten into the quantized onboarding path and adds the CI thresholds.

alex: Can you also dump 50 worst queries for manual annotation? I'll take 25.

maya: Will upload CSV to drive and tag you. link: https://drive.redwood.ai/embeds/q4_0-pca-fails-1749801123.csv

kevin: Thanks — this is a good pattern. Long-term we should track quality by user-cohort and downstream recall (help center retrieval + chat retrieval). For now, shipping q8_0 + canaryed q4_0+PCA seems safe. :thumbsup:

sophia: I'll add a notebook that visualizes before/after PCA whitened embeddings for a handful of queries. Might help explain to PMs.

maya: Putting tasks in Jira now. Thanks everyone. :rocket:
